notes: Summary: Large EU-based rail operator evaluating Redwood Private VPC + on-prem air-gapped variant for safety-critical command-and-control assistants and maintenance diagnostics.
Primary ask: fully offline deployment that can run in Aurora's air-gapped datacenters (no persistent egress). Full KMS/HSM integration, signed model artifacts, and tamper-evident audit logs.
Stakeholders: CTO (evan.muller@aurorarailworks.com), Head of OT Security (marie.leconte@aurorarailworks.com), Procurement lead (tom.haswell@aurorarailworks.com).
Quote from OT Security: 'We cannot accept any solution that requires outbound internet for model telemetry. Auditability and key custody are non-negotiable.'

Model preferences: prefer to use Redwood-verified open model family; require model provenance + signed weights; ability to pin model versions per environment; quantized options suggested for lower-latency on local GPUs.

Workload profile: mixed — interactive chat for control-room assistants (low-latency, strict determinism), batch embeddings for nightly indexing of engineering documents, reranking for incident logs search.
Latency targets: chat p95 < 200ms token-level; end-to-end response for short prompts < 500ms. Throughput: 50 concurrent chat sessions at peak; nightly embedding job ~5M docs over 6 hours.
Cost sensitivity: enterprise budget available but procurement wants clear unit economics and a predictable capacity contract (Dedicated + Private combo).

Security checklist items requested: SSO (SAML) with Azure AD, audit logging to customer's SIEM via syslog/S3 (no SaaS telemetry), KMS integration with AWS CloudHSM or on-prem HSM, FIPS-140 validation, data residency (EU-only), retention policy enforcement (7 years for incident logs), immutable audit exports.

Operational constraints: deployment must integrate with Aurora's OpenShift clusters and their internal GPU pool; customer will provide air-gapped OS image builds and offline storage for model artifacts; Redwood engineer on-site for first-week install preferred.

POC ask: 6-week POC — week1 prep/security workshop, week2 install & smoke, weeks3-5 workload testing (chat + embeddings), week6 security handover + runbook. POC success criteria = pass OT Security checklist + throughput/latency SLOs.
